title: Lines of Symmetry Worksheets
intro: Teach symmetry by checking whether a fold makes the entire shape match.
html:
Teaching notes for parents and teachers

How to teach it

Fold paper shapes or use tracing paper. Test proposed lines against the outline as well as the area on each side.

Example to work through together

Use the model below as you explain the example. Have your student point to the quantities as you discuss them.

Square: four lines of symmetry.
One vertical, one horizontal, and two diagonals.

Cut out a paper square and test each fold. Open the paper after every fold so the original shape remains easy to see.

Ask your student

Would every point on one half match a point on the other?

If your student needs help

If the student chooses any line that halves the area, compare it with an actual fold.

Choosing and using the worksheet

This sheet reuses one original square and one original non-square rectangle. New numbers keeps these same two diagrams; it does not create new shapes. Draw directly on each diagram.
